title: Exercise authenticated marker rewrites and expose the joined rotation floor gap
detail: Three fictional native cases use the ordinary writer-on artifact426. Reuse the unchanged existing production membership/removal helper: both original and joined owners perform membership and history progress saves with reservation interruption and stale-compare controls; each separately retains a lost removal commit reply, resumes exactly, interrupts rotation saving and key activation, then activates, edits, undoes and cold-reopens offline. Freshly MAC-authenticate marker/retained-reading floors after every bounded step. Separately run all three against423’s already-frozen sealed retained-installation fixture, asserting independent reading floor1. This second arm covers a valid dense retained reading instead of assuming that a marked native store implies a marked reading. All case120s deadlines, native permits, cryptographic and comparison checks stay.

The retained-reading arm passes progress/history on both owners (24,926ms) and original removal (22,389ms), but Joined removal fails before its declared activation fault: StorageCompatibilityError at inspectInboundSteps, reached through activateAccountRotation’s validation. It correctly refuses a dense stored receipt because the rotation context omits the freshly authenticated floor. This is a real uncovered valid-format path, not acceptance and not an expected negative fault. No guard is bypassed. Per the operator’s latest direction, the next bounded repair may propagate that existing floor without changing trust/format. Static review enumerates34 mutation calls through exactly the two existing native marker CAS homes; both check monotonicity before storage and at native commit, with Joined checking the reading floor independently. All1,610 previous runtime/protocol/test/configuration files and all449 census source hashes remain exact. One new required family adds two declarations expanding to three runtime cases; inventory731files/725required, all old obligations unchanged. summary: The ordinary floor rewrite/removal lifecycles pass. The independently marked retained-reading control reveals a missing authenticated encoding floor in rotation validation; freeze this counterexample for the next in-scope repair.
limitations: Stage3.2 remains blocked on that real rotation compatibility defect; the extra retained-reading run is red and stays recorded. This is correctness evidence, not a gate, RAM result, Docker rollback proof or release candidate. Marker routing census is not semantic authority evidence. No canonical runtime or old helper/test change, trust/format/server/wire/budget/limit/gate/deadline/default change, commit, publication or deployment. B fairness/past-index, same-tree writer-off images and Stage5/6 remain.
decisionTitle: Test the independent reading floor rather than infer it from native marker activation
decision: Keep separate ordinary and marked-retained-reading observations. The latter must use a valid authenticated sealed reading and every old verification guard. The joined rotation reader’s missing context floor is repaired by copying the already authenticated marker selection, never by granting floor1 to arbitrary receipts or catching its refusal. Preserve the failing native attempt before implementing the separate repair. The latest operator instruction permits continuation for a failure fixable within existing guards.
next: Repair activateAccountRotation’s missing authenticated context floor, review every other InboundContext builder for the same omission, rerun both lifecycle arms and the full-unit checkpoint. Then finish B fairness/past-index and same-tree writer-off Docker rollback; continue automatically.
